author: Baila Eve Zisman
title: Maris Shriver, JFK's Niece, Calls GOP Bill To Rename The Kennedy Center After Trump 'Insane' - NewsBreak
text: Maria Shriver , the former First Lady of California and John F. Kennedy’s niece, has denounced the GOP bill that seeks to rename the Kennedy Center, founded in 1971 , after President Donald Trump . Rep. Bob Onder (R-Missouri) introduced a bill earlier this month – entitled the “Make Entertainment Great Again Act” – which would “designate the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts as the ‘Donald J. Trump Center for the Performing Arts’.” Onder proclaimed, “I cannot think of a more ubiquitous symbol of American exceptionalism in the arts, entertainment, and popular culture at large than President Trump.” Onder’s proposal comes just one week after Republicans proposed naming the opera house at the Kennedy Center after First Lady Melania Trump . On July 28, Shriver reposted a report on the matter, commenting, “This is insane. It makes my blood boil. It’s so ridiculous, so petty, so small-minded. Truly, what is this about? It’s always about something. ‘Let’s get rid of the Rose Garden. Let’s rename the Kennedy Center.’ What’s next?” In February, Trump said that he intended to pave a portion of the White House’s iconic Rose Garden so that it resembled his patio at Mar-a-Lago. Trump took control of the Kennedy Center within the first few weeks of his second term , naming himself its chair, effectively ousting David Rubinstein , and nixing all so-called “woke” policies. Although the Center has traditionally maintained a bipartisan approach on its board, Trump almost immediately fired all those appointed to the board by Joe Biden . Last week, Kennedy’s grandson, Jack Schlossberg, ripped the idea on Instagram, writing, “Plain reading of the statute makes clear — You cant do that.” Schlossberg even cited a 1983 federal law that details, “No additional memorials or plaques in the nature of memorials shall be designated or installed in the public areas of the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts.” Trump’s Big Beautiful Bill Act, passed earlier this month, provided almost $257 million allocated to the Kennedy Center for renovations.
